newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporates maintain focus on cable sector.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporates maintain focus on cable sector.

text.p: Negative sentiment about the cable industry continued to impact the U.S. investment grade corporate bond market and spilled over into the high-yield sector in midday trading, according to market players.
"The focus remains on cable with some noise and a little widening in the sector," said one trader.
Among investment grade cable credits, TCI Communications debt traded wider by another five basis points in morning trade.
Viacom Inc debt held steady after widening approximately five basis points yesterday.
In the high-yield sector, MobileMedia Communications traded off by another 1/2 a point, traders said.
Overall, the high-yield market was off by approximately 1/2 a point, market players said. One trader speculated weakness in the general market was a result of a heavy new issue calendar.
Seperately, an announcement by Stratosphere Corp early today that the troubled casino was unlikely to make its November 15 coupon payment pushed prices down across the gaming sector as well.
"Clearly, a high-profile deterioration of one company will make investors more skittish and spreads will widen accordingly," said Steve Patricola, high-yield gaming analyst at CS First Boston Corp.

Traders noted Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts 11-1/4 percent mortgage notes of 2006 were bid at 94-3/4 in midday, down from 96.5 in early morning trade. The $1.2 billion issue is considered a bellwether for the casino sector because of its large size. "If you want to short Atlantic City and the casino sector, this bond is a good whipping boy for that," said one trader.
Turning to the high-grade sector, the primary market remained the prime subject of investor interest, as secondary trading across most sectors remained muted.
Early Thursday, Banc One sold $500 million in 30-year 7.625 percent bonds at 99.191 to yield 7.694 percent, according to syndicate officials.
In what is expected to be a hot upcoming issue, Husky Oil Ltd plans to debut in the debt market by selling $500 million of senior notes and debentures in early November.
The deal, which is rated Baa3/BBB, is expected to generate considerable investor interest because of the paucity of higher yielding new issues in this credit range in recent months, dealers said.
The Canadian oil company chose BT Securities Corp and CIBC Wood Gundy Securities as co-lead managers for the transaction.
